MemArchitect splits memory lifecycle control from model weights and enforces decay, conflict, and privacy policies. Governed memory beat unmanaged memory in their agentic tests.
arxiv-2603-18530: Basu and Chakraborty test whether large language models change verdicts when only names, credentials, or wording change. Their ICE-Guard framework swaps these features across 3,000 short cases in ten high-stakes fields. They test 11 models and find authority bias and framing bias beat demographic bias. Finance shows the strongest authority bias. A fix that splits feature extraction from a fixed rubric cuts flip rates sharply. Checks on real COMPAS data suggest the test may understate real bias.
arxiv-2603-18630: The ATLAS Collaboration combines LHC data to bound unusual couplings among four gauge bosons. The inputs cover vector-boson scattering in many final states plus a tri-boson study. All data come from proton-proton collisions at 13 TeV. A field theory frame with dimension-8 terms sets the search terms. Results come as 68 and 95 percent confidence ranges for Wilson coefficients. Fits run with one or two free values, with and without unitarity limits. Fits over all values at once are also reported.
arxiv-2603-18930: Zhu and Liu prove that a key equation tied to the AKNS spectral problem has a unique solution. The equation can be turned into an integral form whose kernel swings with a space variable. They split the work to control how the integral settles. A new operator helps show the solution exists under a small-norm rule. They then extend a dressing method to build AKNS solutions from this data. They also show the map from data to potential changes in a stable, bounded way.
arxiv-2603-19230: Akbaba and co-authors map the old, alpha-rich disk of the Milky Way by chemistry, age, and orbit. They use subgiant stars with sharp ages and element data from LAMOST and Gaia. Maps in orbit space show clear trends in iron, alpha share, and age. These trends are far sharper than maps in raw motion space. Older groups show trends much like the younger disk, though weaker. The pattern points to growth from the inside out and from flat to thick.
arxiv-2603-19330: Johnson and co-authors forecast chip benchmark scores with a learned model instead of slow simulators. Cycle-level simulators take too long to run full suites and are hard to keep up. Their PAI reads a trace of program traits that do not depend on chip details. A layered LSTM model then predicts the speed metrics for the run. On the SPEC CPU 2017 suite, mean error in cycles per instruction is about 9 percent. The full suite takes under three minutes to project, far faster than prior methods.
arxiv-2603-19530: Cote and Sun design a two-layer dispatch system that adds carbon accounting to power markets. The first layer picks generation at least cost, as markets do now. The second layer cuts emissions within that least-cost set. From this setup they define locational marginal emissions for each grid node. They prove results like the classic welfare theorems of economics. A carbon footprint theorem shows node accounts sum to total physical emissions. Case studies on a Texas grid model check the theory.
arxiv-2603-19930: Nechi and co-authors learn beam codebooks for millimeter-wave and terahertz systems with reinforcement learning. Fixed codebooks often perform poorly without a line of sight or on limited hardware. Their multi-agent method learns codebooks from environmental feedback alone, with no channel knowledge needed first. They compare three off-policy algorithms: DDPG, TD3, and SAC. Simulations test how each copes with hardware flaws and noisy feedback. SAC gave the best beamforming gains and stability in non-line-of-sight cases, even under severe impairments.
arxiv-2603-20030: Delecroix, Fontaine, and de Mesmay bound the size of k-irreducible triangulations of surfaces. A triangulation is k-irreducible when every non-contractible curve has length at least k. Contracting any edge must break that property. They prove such a triangulation of a genus g surface has order k squared times g triangles. The bound is optimal, so no sharper general bound exists. It greatly improves the earlier bound of Gao, Richter, and Seymour. That bound grew far faster in both k and g.
arxiv-2603-20230: Abouelazm and co-authors give self driving reinforcement learning a ranked set of goals instead of one blended score. Safety, efficiency, and comfort often conflict on the road. Weighted sums hide those priorities and can yield unsafe policies. Their preordered framework keeps a hierarchy over reward parts. A new comparison, quantile dominance, judges action return distributions without collapsing them. An algorithm then keeps the actions that stay non dominated per goal. Built on implicit quantile networks, tests in Carla showed fewer collisions and better success rates.
arxiv-2603-20330: Ghosh studies how two localization effects compete in a non-Hermitian SSH chain. The skin effect piles states at one edge, while quasiperiodic disorder traps them in place. Ghosh maps the full phase diagram using exact diagonalization and transfer matrices. Five regimes appear, including a new one with reentrant partial delocalization. Moderate disorder breaks up skin buildup before localizing every state. Disorder also unwinds the complex spectral loops and destroys point-gap topology. The skin effect crushes entanglement, which strong disorder partly restores.
arxiv-2603-20430: Arca Sedda and co-authors model how black hole binaries form across cosmic settings. Mergers seen by LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA can arise from isolated pairs or crowded clusters. Their B-POP code follows both channels in young, globular, and nuclear clusters. It folds in star formation history and metallicity change over time. Predicted merger rates, 17.5 to 24.1 per cubic gigaparsec yearly, match observations. Isolated binaries dominate below 20 solar masses in primary mass. Dynamically built mergers take over at higher masses. Their mass and spin patterns also fit current data.
arxiv-2603-20930: Malarkkan and co-authors select features that stay valid when data distributions shift. Most methods chase accuracy on one distribution and pick spurious features that later fail. Their CGDFS method treats feature choice as sampling from a posterior over subsets. That posterior favors low error plus low variance across environments. A diffusion model supplies a prior over plausible selection masks. Guided annealed Langevin sampling then mixes the prior with the stability goal. Tests on real data with shifts show more stable, transferable feature sets than sparsity, tree, and stability baselines.
arxiv-2603-21130: Šfiligoj and co-authors review multilayer networks in public transport research and set an agenda for the field. Single layer networks often fail to capture real transport systems in enough detail. Multilayer networks stack linked layers, which suits systems with mixed elements and relations. The literature on them in transport is scattered, with no shared terms or agreed methods. They present the basic formalism, then survey and classify how transport systems get modeled as multilayer networks. They close with a research agenda for the coming decade.
arxiv-2603-21230: Papoutsellis and co-authors expand the Core Imaging Library with a modular framework for stochastic optimisation in inverse problems. The library solves imaging problems such as CT with a plug-in design. The new framework lets researchers combine building blocks to form many stochastic algorithms, instead of coding each one as a black box. They show it on real X-ray CT and PET reconstruction data. The suite aims to make testing and benchmarking stochastic methods easier.
arxiv-2603-21430: Wang and co-authors present DomAgent, a coding agent for tasks that need specialized domain knowledge. General language models often fail such tasks because the knowledge is rare in their training data. DomAgent retrieves help through DomRetriever, which mixes top-down knowledge-graph reasoning with bottom-up case-based reasoning. The loop gathers structured facts and past cases before code is written. On the DS-1000 benchmark and on real truck software tasks, DomAgent let small open models close much of the gap with large closed ones.
arxiv-2603-21530: Chen and co-authors generate test cases for database systems with help from language models and Monte Carlo tree search. Fuzzers work well but need heavy manual tuning for each proprietary SQL dialect. Lightweight models, common inside companies, often write invalid queries and quickly run out of variety. Their MIST framework builds a feature tree and uses error feedback to guide valid, diverse query synthesis. Tree search then mutates seed queries toward deeper code paths. Coverage rose sharply over the best baseline on three systems.
arxiv-2603-21830: Sultana and co-authors study how rural Bangladeshi communities teach facts and values through narrative performance. Data storytelling tools often grow from modern visualization norms that can sideline low-literacy audiences. Over ten months in three villages, the team watched forms like Puthi, Bhandari Gaan, and Pot music at work. Performers mix many voices and moral frames in one show. They blend fact, feeling, and beauty, and adapt as technology and audiences change. The findings offer design lessons for data stories that respect local culture.
arxiv-2603-22430: Deb and co-authors add a way to tune a trained policy at the moment it acts. Offline reinforcement learning fixes a policy from stored data before deployment. Their method pairs that policy with a learned world model that can be differentiated. Gradients then flow through imagined rollouts, so the policy can adjust on the fly. On D4RL control benchmarks the authors report steady gains over strong baselines. They also cut the cost with a cheaper sampler that keeps most of the benefit.
arxiv-2603-22930: Fauvel and co-authors introduce CMA-Unfold, an open-source tool for stacked calorimeter detectors. These detectors record depth-dose profiles from bursts of high-energy photons and particles. Recovering the true energy spectrum is an ill-posed inverse problem. Noise and response uncertainty make it harder. Their method uses covariance matrix adaptation, an evolution strategy, to fit spectra. It imposes no fixed parametric shape on the spectrum. Tests recover complex spectral shapes with high fidelity. The tool tolerates percent-level errors in single detector layers.
arxiv-2603-23230: Battagliola and six co-authors study the Linear Equivalence Problem for error-correcting codes. The problem asks whether a linear map can turn one code into another. Its permutation-only cousin drew interest as a base for post-quantum schemes like LESS. A recent method used the Schur product to crack many easy cases of that cousin. The team extends the idea with power codes, Frobenius maps, and Hermitian hulls. They map out classes of easy linear cases. They also give a sharper reduction to the permutation problem.
arxiv-2603-23530: Mittal studies why language models drop formatting orders while busy with hard tasks. She frames the slip as a prospective memory failure, borrowed from mind science. Across three model families and 8,000 prompts, rule following falls as task load grows. End-of-answer rules suffer most, with drops near half. Avoidance rules hold up far better. A clearer frame plus a trailing reminder restores most lost compliance. The load cuts both ways: one model's math score fell from 93 to 27 percent under format rules.
arxiv-2603-23630: Friedl, Hirsch, and Kegel give a full proof of Markov's theorem on the homeomorphism problem. The problem asks whether two manifolds share the same shape. Markov showed no algorithm can settle that question in general. The same work yields manifolds that no test can recognize. Such rebels exist in every dimension above three. The note lays out the proof in detail for modern readers.
arxiv-2603-23730: Paul, Patterson, and Bouguila tune 3D foundation models without bolting on adapters. Point cloud giants adapt poorly on scarce data: full tuning overfits and drifts. Adapter tricks add parts that slow each run. Their momentum-consistency route tunes part of the encoder while a momentum rule guards the base skills. Two variants add unlabeled data help or prune layers for speed. Tests on shape tasks beat prior methods, with few-shot gains over three points.
arxiv-2603-23830: Ma and Konomi propose example-based scaffolding for beginner programming in the age of generative AI. AI can hand students working code, which invites copying and skips reasoning. Their approach gives scaffold examples that share the target task's reasoning pattern but use a new context. Students must transfer the pattern rather than copy the answer. The authors give a two-part taxonomy and design guidelines. Their prototype, CodeExemplar, links to auto-graded tasks and drew early feedback from a class pilot.
arxiv-2603-25230: Liang and Pun fix a blind spot in attacks that warp images to fool AI models. Such transformation attacks transfer well for plain classification. They flop on tasks with shaped labels, like segmentation and detection. The cause is drift: warp the image but not its label map, and the training signal points the wrong way. Their Spatial Alignment Framework warps labels in step with inputs. Attack strength jumps: average segmentation scores fall by half or more on two sets, and detection scores drop hard on COCO.
arxiv-2603-25330: Polovinkin and co-authors predict the traits of molten metal-salt mixes for calcium making, using learned atom models. Hot experiments on such melts are slow and costly. The team trains Moment Tensor Potentials on quantum-grade data, then runs molecular dynamics with them. Two systems matter for calcium electrolysis: a calcium-copper melt and a chloride salt mix. The runs reproduce density, heat capacity, conductivity, and flow traits across heat and mix ranges. Errors stay within twenty percent of lab values, which validates the approach.
arxiv-2603-26130: Kumar introduces SWE-PRBench, a benchmark that grades AI code review against human feedback. It holds 350 pull requests with human-marked issues as ground truth. Eight frontier models are tested in three context setups, from diff only to full files. The models catch just 15 to 31 percent of the issues humans flagged. More context hurts every model, Kumar reports. Failures cluster in contextual issues once file content is added. Short, summarized prompts beat longer full-context ones. The top four models tie, with a clear gap to the rest.
arxiv-2603-26230: Nagamiya traces the early history that led to the atomic bomb. He focuses on scientists who faced hard moral choices about the weapon. Some spoke out against its use on Japan. Others tried to warn a Japanese physicist, hoping to limit the harm. Still others felt deep remorse after the attacks. He also covers one person who lived through the bombing, and asks how ethics should guide research in the future.
arxiv-2603-26430: Smirnova, Dan, and Mayr study calls to order in the German Bundestag as a marker of incivility. Parliamentary clashes shape laws and public debate, yet calls to order have drawn little systematic study. The team builds a rule-based method to spot and annotate them in speeches. Their dataset spans 72 years of debates with a first classification of what triggers a call. They find insults to individuals are the top trigger, and that men and opposition members draw more calls.
arxiv-2603-26530: Allison develops a theory of how self-organising cell groups can control gene activity. Multicellular self-organisation drives development, yet a full theory is still missing. Basic cell traits can break the usual modelling routes, he notes. Starting from broad biological first principles, he frames cell links as dynamic graphs that shift over time. The view grows out of earlier work on Escherichia coli colonies. He argues the frame can guide lab work, simulations, and efforts to engineer living systems.
arxiv-2603-26830: Lauziere and co-authors build a regression framework that measures how each prompt part affects language model scores. The method fits statistical models that link prompt portions to task results. They test it on Mistral-7B and GPT-OSS-20B solving a simple arithmetic problem. The regressions explain 72 and 77 percent of performance variation. Wrong example answers hurt both models. Positive and negative instructions showed mixed, contradictory effects across the two models.
arxiv-2603-26930: Wang and co-authors introduce In Your Own Words, a framework for finding themes in free-text survey answers. Open responses carry nuance that fixed questions miss, yet resist standard statistics. The framework extracts structured, interpretable themes from the raw text. The team tests it on identity descriptions from 1,004 U.S. participants. Its themes proved more coherent than those from earlier computational methods. The themes suggest new survey questions on belonging and identity fluidity. They also expose gaps between self-identified and perceived identities.
arxiv-2603-27130: Mao and co-authors measure AI-generated code inside real-world software repositories at large scale. Lab studies use small synthetic tasks, leaving open how AI code looks in production projects. The team compares AI-assisted and human-written code across many metrics. Code-level measures cover structure, style, complexity, and security quality. Commit-level measures cover size, frequency, and later stability. Real-world differences on code metrics proved smaller than lab studies suggested. Security quality varied notably across programming languages. New ground includes duplication rates and commit stability patterns.
arxiv-2603-27330: Areias and Picado study continuity and openness for maps between locales through Galois adjunctions. Four adjoint setups swap images and preimages with closure and interior operators. Those adjunctions characterize meet-preserving maps, localic maps, and open maps in two senses. Working in the concrete language of sublocales keeps the reasoning elementary. Open localic maps then get a detailed revisit. A new proof of the Joyal-Tierney open mapping theorem emerges from the framework. Interchange laws between preimages, images, closure, and interior close the study.
arxiv-2603-27430: Sohail and co-authors speed up multiscale tests of rubber-like materials. Full atom-level runs are far too slow for large parts. Their method trains a neural operator on atom-level data. The operator maps strain history to stress at each point. It slots into a standard finite-element solver. Learned states inside it capture memory effects. Heat transfer across temperatures is also handled. Tests on polyurea match lab-grade models well. Large impact tests become feasible at last.
arxiv-2603-27730: Sohrabi studies rings whose additive group is finitely generated. Such rings are called FDZ-rings or FDZ-algebras. They need not be commutative or have a unit. He gives tests for quasi finite axiomatizability. Links to bi-interpretability with the integers also appear. Rings sharing the same first-order theory get described. Those portraits hold under stated constraints on the base ring. The work extends an earlier joint paper.
arxiv-2603-28030: Good and Linder present an exact model of a moving mirror in flat spacetime that mimics Hawking radiation from a black hole. The mirror's acceleration grows without bound, yet the total energy it radiates stays finite. In the black hole version, that trait means zero surface gravity. The authors work out the particle and energy spectra and the matching spacetime metric in closed form. The model mixes traits of normal and extremal black holes.
arxiv-2603-28130: Li and nine co-authors release MDPBench, the first benchmark for parsing documents in many languages and real conditions. Parsers are usually tested on clean digital pages in a few big languages. MDPBench holds 3,400 document images in 17 languages, mixing digital files and photos under varied conditions. Closed models held up fairly well, but open models dropped sharply on photographed pages and non-Latin scripts. The gaps point to concrete fixes for fairer parsing tools.
arxiv-2603-28230: Kobayashi studies the electromagnetic duality of the two-dimensional Z2 toric code, a symmetry swapping its electric and magnetic particles. He proves this duality cannot be realized exactly by a Clifford circuit as an internal Z2 symmetry. The proof covers symmetries with a coarse translation invariance for odd step sizes. So an exact Z2 version must use non-Clifford gates, while Clifford versions need a larger Z2^m algebra. The result links duality to the Clifford hierarchy.
arxiv-2603-28530: Mudi and three co-authors test why supercurrents in InAs-Al Josephson junctions come back at high sideways magnetic fields. Such re-entrance could herald a topological phase or a 0-to-pi switch, both prized for quantum devices. Some junctions match those expected marks. Yet the same patterns can arise from mode interference in a disordered link, with no topology at all. Simulations of a rippled weak link under in-plane fields reproduce the effect, urging care in reading the signal.
arxiv-2603-28730: Schroeder and co-authors introduce SOLE-R1, a video-language model that serves as the sole reward for robot reinforcement learning. Strong evaluator models can fail under partial observability and reward hacking. SOLE-R1 reads raw video and a language goal, then reasons step by step over time and space. It outputs dense estimates of task progress as rewards. A synthesis pipeline created training traces tied to continuous progress labels. Across four simulated settings and a real robot, robots learned unseen tasks from scratch. SOLE-R1 succeeded on 24 unseen tasks.
arxiv-2603-28930: Balzer, Khowaja, and Fuchs build a model to judge the economic cost of group testing in a pandemic. Testing each person alone is often infeasible, so samples are pooled. Standard cost views count only costs and miss income lost to quarantine and workplace disruption. Their model joins test counts at optimized pool sizes with German income data. Monte Carlo tests on COVID-19 show the best algorithm choice changes once income losses count. Direct cost views understate total cost. Shorter quarantine methods win, even if they need more tests.
arxiv-2603-29630: Herzog and co-authors introduce BigEarthNet.txt, a large image-text dataset for Earth observation. Vision-language models lag on remote sensing data for lack of such datasets. Their set pairs radar and multispectral Sentinel images, over 464,000 in all. It carries 9.6 million text annotations of several kinds. Captions anchor land cover classes in geography and context. Question-answer pairs and referring expressions add more task types. A hand-checked benchmark split tests current models. Fine-tuning on the dataset lifted scores across all tasks.
arxiv-2603-29830: Adams, Jefremovas, and Michels classify neutron scattering patterns from magnetic vortex ensembles. They study dilute spherical nanoparticles that host vortex states. A linear vortex model gives an averaged spin-flip cross section formula. The patterns fall into four symmetry regimes. Some show four-fold or two-fold order, while one is an isotropic ring. Analytic lines bound these regimes in vortex parameter space. A nonlinear profile check shows the regions hold up.
arxiv-2604-00130: Huang and three colleagues propose Hi-CoT, a reasoning scheme that splits a language model's chain of thought into layered substeps. Planning instructions alternate with step-by-step execution, helping models handle long reasoning chains without losing logical thread. Across varied models and mathematics benchmarks, average accuracy rises 6.2 percent, reaching about 61 percent on some models and tasks. Reasoning traces also shrink by about 14 percent against ordinary chain-of-thought prompting, with the best results when models follow the layered structure strictly.
arxiv-2604-00230: Rupa identifies a stable predictor for neural collapse: collapse sets in when mean feature norm reaches a critical value specific to each model and dataset. Crossing below that value precedes collapse onset by a mean 62 epochs, and an intervention test confirms it as a stable attractor. Depth affects collapse speed unevenly, activation shapes speed and the critical value, weight decay splits into three regimes, and width speeds collapse while shifting the value by at most 13 percent. ResNet-20 on MNIST shows the strongest architecture effect, 458 percent against 68 percent on CIFAR-10.
arxiv-2604-00830: Lou and colleagues introduce Meta-TTL, a framework that learns self-improvement policies for language agents instead of hand-crafting them. An inner loop runs test-time learning across episodes, while an outer loop meta-trains across tasks using a balanced improvement score to weigh contributions. Tested on Jericho, WebArena-Lite, and related benchmarks, Meta-TTL beats the strongest baseline. Gains reach up to 23 percent on in-distribution tasks and 27 percent on out-of-distribution tasks.
arxiv-2604-00930: Takahashi and team revisit the first Vicsek model. They show its angle-based update rule changes with global phase shifts, at the level of angle steps, when built with the principal-value arctangent. The phase transition seen in the first paper goes away when the global phase is chosen on the fly. The work doubts the common belief that it reflects natural breaking of O(2) spinning symmetry.
arxiv-2604-01030: Liu and team introduce Diff3R, bridging feed-forward prediction and test-time optimization for 3D Gaussian Splatting. A differentiable optimization layer in the training loop teaches the network to predict a strong starting point for test-time optimization, not zero-shot. Gradients flow via the Implicit Function Theorem with a matrix-free PCG solver. A data-driven uncertainty model limits parameter changes during optimization, curbing overfitting in under-constrained regions and boosting outlier robustness. The layer is model-agnostic, slotting into feed-forward architectures for pose settings.
arxiv-2604-01330: Staněk and colleagues fuse deepfake speech detectors with an evolutionary search that weighs detection error against system size together. Instead of stacking every detector, they evolve two encodings under NSGA-II: one picks which detectors to average, and one tunes weights for a weighted sum. Tested on ASVspoof 5 with 36 self-supervised detectors, the trade-off fronts beat simple averaging and logistic regression. The weighted version reaches 2.37 percent equal error rate while matching top accuracy with only half the parameters.
arxiv-2604-01430: Chaudhry, Thiagarajan and Lampinen characterize latent generalization, where in-weights learning struggles with deductive reasoning over internalized knowledge, exemplified by the reversal curse. They study how models can be taught to use test-time compute, or thinking, to improve latent generalization. They train models with reinforcement learning from correctness feedback to produce long chains-of-thought. It generalizes to new knowledge with no reinforcement learning performed. On pure reversal tasks, thinking does not unlock direct knowledge inversion, but generate-and-verify ability lifts models well above chance.
arxiv-2604-01730: Grasev applies Koopman operator ideas to controlling a two-spool turbofan engine. A component model built from physics generates training data and validates control. A tuned extended dynamic mode method for spool speeds and the engine pressure ratio yields one Koopman model reusable. From the model he builds an adaptive predictive controller with an observer, comparing it against feedback linear control with and without an integrator. Nonlinear output limits become linear constraints in the predictive controller, best under varying flight, while pressure ratio control improves thrust.
arxiv-2604-01830: Dogoulis and Cordy propose a physics-informed reinforcement learning framework for power grid topology control, a hard problem with fast-growing actions and costly evaluation. They combine semi-Markov control with a Gibbs prior encoding system physics, deciding only in risky regimes. A graph neural network surrogate predicts overload risk, building a Gibbs prior selecting candidates and reweighting logits. The method cuts exploration and simulation cost while keeping a policy flexible, matching oracle performance at 6 times the speed, reaching 94.6 percent of oracle reward, and beating a PPO baseline.
arxiv-2604-02130: Ostmeyer offers a concise handbook for handling fermion determinants exactly in quantum Monte Carlo. Working with the fermion matrix in the sausage, or Green's function, form, he matches method to volume. Dense matrix operations give a stable route for small volumes at very low temperatures, while a sparse approach scales well for large volumes. The guide is not a review but a practical map, stressing that varied regimes need varied tools.
arxiv-2604-02230: Gourabathina and colleagues teach language models when to abstain by checking whether the model answered the wrong question. Their Trace Inversion method first generates a reasoning trace, then reconstructs the most likely query behind it from the trace alone. A low match between the original query and the reconstructed query flags the answer for abstention. Across four frontier models and nine abstention datasets, the method beats rivals in 33 of 36 settings.
arxiv-2604-02530: Silva proposes AQ-Stacker, a hybrid quantum-classical method for matrix multiplication, the core workload of modern machine learning. It caches state-preparation blocks outside the main loop and adapts its run pattern, from sequential stacking to wide parallelism, to the qubits on hand. A new concentration bound, the Entropy Dividend, steadies noisy weight estimates, and tests reach 96 percent accuracy on handwritten digits.
arxiv-2604-03230: Rao and colleagues map young stars in the halo of M82, a starburst galaxy with a prototypical outflow, using Hubble and Subaru observations. They find widespread extraplanar stars younger than 630 million years, including arc features about 5 kiloparsecs south and a trail reaching about 20 kiloparsecs east. The halo formed about 4 million solar masses of stars in that span, tied to outflow bursts in the disk.
arxiv-2604-03430: Fleming and colleagues propose Cognitive Fabric Nodes, a middleware layer that sits between agents in multi-agent systems instead of passing messages blindly. The fabric treats memory as an active substrate feeding topology choice, semantic grounding, security enforcement, and prompt transformation, each tuned by learning. Tests on HotPotQA and MuSiQue show gains over 10 percent on both datasets versus direct agent-to-agent communication.
arxiv-2604-03530: Omar proves that the limit points of real roots of all-terminal reliability polynomials are just the range from minus one to zero, plus one. That resolves a guess of Brown and McMullin. The proof hinges on showing that real reliability roots of edge-swap graphs are dense. It builds on a multi-edge graph thickness result of Brown and Colbourn.
arxiv-2604-04230: Mouzouni tracks how expert routing shifts across training in two open mixture-of-experts models. A single congestion measure reveals three stages. First comes an early surge toward balanced load. Then experts specialize while balance holds steady. Finally balance gives way to quality as experts diverge. The pattern, hidden in finished models, shows early training favouring balance and late training favouring quality.
arxiv-2604-04330: Chen and colleagues build a hardware-aware training pipeline for vision transformers on silicon-photonic near-sensor accelerators. They first measure noise in microring-resonator banks, covering fabrication variation, thermal drift and amplitude noise, then turn those readings into variance proxies. Their Chance-Constrained Training enforces logit margins to limit attention rank flips, joined by a noise-aware LayerNorm that steadies feature statistics without touching the optical schedule. Hardware tests with photonic banks restore near-clean accuracy under realistic noise, with no on-site learning or extra optical operations.
arxiv-2604-04830: Krajicek rules out the strong feasible disjunction property for strong proof systems, under two hypotheses. A proof system has the property when a short proof of a disjunction of formulas sharing no atoms yields a short proof of one disjunct. Its size is bounded by a power of the first proof. He combines work by Ilango and Ren and colleagues with a 2007 gadget generator. The two hypotheses posit a class E language needing exponential-size circuits even with an NP oracle, and a P-over-poly demi-bit per Rudich.
arxiv-2604-04930: Hosseini and four colleagues tackle overthinking in large reasoning models, where long chains of thought cost compute and can even worsen answers. They track confidence in intermediate answers and find a pattern: correct paths often reach high-confidence answers early, while wrong paths ramble with shaky confidence. Their CoDE-Stop method uses those confidence dynamics to halt reasoning at the right moment. It needs no extra training and slots easily into existing pipelines, aiming to save compute while keeping answers sound.
arxiv-2604-05030: Vishwakarma and Agostino introduce Phase-Associative Memory, a complex-valued sequence model for language that draws on quantum logic rather than classical Boolean summing. Tests suggest the meaning of a phrase is unfixed before interpretation, not simply the sum of its parts. Reading, in this view, makes meaning real under genuine context, a process that fits quantum rules better than old ways assuming parts split. Their model stores outer products of complex token codes, found through a paired inner product, building a state of phase-linked links across a sequence.
arxiv-2604-05130: Chen and six co-authors propose Vulnsage, a multi-agent framework for exploit generation with grasp and reflection. Open-source code is widely used in modern software, introducing safety flaws. Static analysis tools can find flaws at scale, yet they generate huge reports with many false alarms. Exploit generation aims to confirm truth by building an exploit. Methods based on fuzzing or symbolic execution face path reach problems. Language models show promise for grasping flaws and making exploits. How to use them remains an open question.
arxiv-2604-05830: López and four colleagues cut demographic bias in wake-up word detection by training without demographic labels. Using the OK Aura database, they test data augmentation and distillation from foundational speech models, reserving labels for evaluation only. One method cuts predictive disparity by about 40 percent for sex, about 84 percent for age, and about 40 percent for accent.
arxiv-2604-05930: Xu and nine colleagues test whether large vision-language models get multimodal puns, jokes where image and text jointly set up two meanings. Their MultiPun set pairs varied puns with tricky non-pun lookalikes, and most models fail to tell the two apart. Prompt tweaks and model-level fixes lift F1 scores by 16.5 percent on average, pointing to cross-modal reasoning gaps.
arxiv-2604-06030: Byun, Hongsoo Kim, and Seunghyun Kim prove global C^{1,alpha} regularity for viscosity solutions of a class of singular and degenerate fully nonlinear elliptic equations. That is a smoothness result for weak solutions. The result holds across the whole domain. They carry oblique boundary conditions, where the boundary rule at each edge point uses a directional derivative at an angle. Their 2026 paper extends earlier findings to a broader class of equations, with the singular case too.
arxiv-2604-06530: Bian and six colleagues test whether a non-topological Z prime string in the minimal 331 model can hold together. Starting from a symmetry-breaking chain rooted in an SU(6) toy model with two Higgs triplets, they perturb the string background and solve the resulting equations numerically. Stability appears only near the semilocal limit, even after tuning Higgs couplings to calm instabilities. That suggests such strings rarely survive in unified theories built on SU(N) with N above five.
arxiv-2604-06630: Mladenov proves that differential graded categories in holomorphic symplectic geometry are all formal. He works with three linked kinds: Lagrangian branes, their quantised forms, and the virtual de Rham kind, all on one such manifold. They turn out formal in this work when localized at orientable compact Kähler Lagrangian submanifolds with pairwise clean intersections. Along the way he defines Kaledin classes of minimal A-infinity categories, which obstruct formality. He also gives a plain test for when flat weakly proper Calabi-Yau differential graded categories are formal.
arxiv-2604-06930: Maroń, Pańtak, and Pachucki present a full theory of muonic hydrogen hyperfine splitting above one part per million. Quantum electrodynamic and recoil shifts are worked out first-hand, while the proton structure shift comes from plain hydrogen hyperfine splitting. The ground-state prediction is 182,626 micro-electronvolts, with an uncertainty of 5 in the last digits.
arxiv-2604-07230: Xu and four colleagues tackle a weak spot in image editing: moved objects often land at the wrong size or place. Their PhyEdit tool adds clear 3D shape and perspective cues to guide edits, trained with both 2D and 3D checks. To train and test it, they release RealManip-40K, a real-world set of paired images with depth labels, plus ManipEval, a test for spatial control. In trials, PhyEdit beats prior tools, even strong closed-source ones, on shape accuracy and consistency.
arxiv-2604-07530: Trišović introduces time-to-peak and lifespan as gauges of language-model obsolescence in science, tracing 62 models across over 108000 citing papers from 2019 to 2025. Separating active adoption from background citation recovers per-model trajectories that raw citation counts hide. Longevity depends more on release timing than on architecture, openness, or scale. Adoption follows an inverted-U curve, rising, peaking, then declining, but that curve is compressing fast: each later release year brings a 27 percent shorter time-to-peak and a 23 percent shorter lifespan.
arxiv-2604-07830: Choudhuri, Bird, Badea, and Sarma ask what AI tools developers want beyond code writing. Developers spend roughly a tenth of their day writing code, yet most AI tooling targets it. A survey of 860 Microsoft developers, read by a human-in-the-loop council of models, yields 22 wanted systems across five task types. For each, the paper names the problem, the hard part, and the limits developers set. Findings point to a growing burden of checking AI output, with calls for earlier quality signals and strict limits on tool powers.
arxiv-2604-07930: Desai and six colleagues improve Walmart sponsored search retrieval by unifying training signals. Fast first-stage retrievers usually learn from user clicks, logged at scale without annotation. Clicks are a flawed proxy for relevance: they may reflect popularity, promotion, visuals, titles, or price rather than query fit. Sponsored search worsens the problem, since ad exposure depends on auctions and advertiser moves, leaving click data sparse by design. Their unified training blends semantic relevance with click signals so retrievers rank items users truly want, not merely items they happened to see.
arxiv-2604-08030: Budde and four colleagues define personalization in recourse as actionability. Recourse offers usable tips for changing bad model outcomes, and prior work studies speed, toughness, and fairness at length. Yet its role stays hidden and vague, with no clear meaning and no careful study of effects on other traits. That spans two sides: hard constraints marking which traits a person can really change, and soft custom limits showing tastes over action values and costs. The paper puts both sides to work for analysis.
arxiv-2604-08230: Deshmukh, Hambarde, and Proença survey cross-domain object detection: progress, pitfalls, and persistent challenges. Object detection models trained on one domain often degrade in unseen target domains, due to shifts in sensing, environments, and data distributions. Despite recent breakthroughs in deep learning-based detection, cross-domain detection remains a critical research area. Existing work remains fragmented, without a unified view of structural challenges behind domain shift or adaptation strategies. The survey gives a comprehensive analysis of cross-domain detection, starting from a formulation highlighting its multi-stage nature.
arxiv-2604-08730: Zhao and four colleagues study winner take all contests on hypergraphs, where pairwise blocking gains multi way link terms from uniform hyper links. Their Lotka-Volterra model yields winner take all, winner share all, and variant winner take all results. Existence, uniqueness, and stability are proved with standard theory and tensor algebra. The final outcome depends little on hyperedge order or coupling structure, instead tracking a few scalar values like blocking ratios and outside inputs, as tests confirm.
arxiv-2604-09030: Qu and colleagues present the NTIRE 2026 Restore Any Image Model challenge, track two, on multi-exposure image fusion in dynamic scenes. Fusing bracketed exposures into high dynamic range images must cope with scene motion, changing light, and handheld camera shake. The benchmark holds 100 training sequences with seven exposure levels and 100 test sequences with five, drawn from real-world conditions. Scoring blends PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS with perceptual quality, efficiency, and reproducibility, and the track drew 114 teams and 987 submissions, with winners cutting fusion artifacts and recovering fine detail.
arxiv-2604-09130: Liao and five colleagues introduce EquiformerV3, a third-generation graph attention transformer that respects three-dimensional rotation symmetry for atom-scale modeling. The new version runs 1.75 times faster through leaner code, adds merged layer normalization, tuned feedforward settings, and attention with a smooth radius cutoff. New SwiGLU-S2 activations bring in many-body effects while keeping strict symmetry and easing sampling over sphere grids. Trained with a denoising side task, the model sets new best results on the OC20, OMat24, and Matbench Discovery benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-09230: Janoš, Orr-Ewing, Curchod, and Slavíček critically assess mixed-reference spin-flip density functional theory, a method prized for photochemistry. It blends single-reference speed with multireference flexibility, but the authors identify two limits. First, its doubly excited configurations cost some singly excited ones, and its triplet reference can abruptly change character when two triplet states nearly coincide. That swap can warp energy curves with jumps or sharp distortions, so the authors offer diagnostics for spotting these faults.
arxiv-2604-09830: Easson presents a seed-to-Kerr-Schild route to Birkhoff rigidity in vacuum gravity. On the orbit space, areal radius determines a scalar, and vacuum equations imply a radial function. Two normalized one-forms are closed, so their null combinations are exact seed forms. Integrating these yields Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates with a Kerr-Schild metric over a flat background. In the stationary optical sector, spherical symmetry compels the inverse optical seed to plus or minus the radius. The seed data reconstruct the Schwarzschild family, pairing Birkhoff rigidity with its converse.
arxiv-2604-09930: Bond and four co-authors report spectroscopy of Kohoutek 1-9, a little-studied nucleus, finding a dwarf barium star. Its spectrum shows strong carbon and s-process features, joining a tiny barium-star group. Progenitors are likely wide binaries: the primary reached the pulsing giant phase, dredged up carbon and s-process elements, and transferred material by wind. The leftover core is now a hot pre-white dwarf ionizing the ejecta, while the barium star dominates. Amateur images show a thin ring, likely orbital-plane ejecta, with the nucleus off-center.
arxiv-2604-10030: Chen, Huang, and Liu present Prompt Relay, a run-time plug-and-play method for fine-grained time control in multi-event video making, needing no design changes. Single prose-style prompts cause sense tangle, with concepts for other moments bleeding as one and hurting text-video match. Prompt Relay adds a penalty to cross-focus so each time segment attends only to its set prompt, letting the model show one. This lifts time prompt match, reduces sense noise, and lifts visual quality, aiding clear tales through timing and shifts.
arxiv-2604-10430: Lin, Ramakrishnan, Goza, Matlack, and Bae test how a tuned wall lining steers wall turbulence. Their defect tuned phononic subsurface acts as a live wall that rings in a narrow band. Even under broad turbulent push, the lining answers narrowly, damping speed swings and cutting drag. Its peak tone drifts off the planned ring pitch once flow and wall truly interact. The phase across panels tracks passing turbulent shapes, a guide for quiet passive flow control.
arxiv-2604-10630: Singh and three colleagues use quantum-mechanical calculations to study the boundary between lithium metal and the Li3OCl solid electrolyte. That junction's stability decides how well solid-state lithium batteries perform. Comparing several interface orientations, they find the most favorable arrangement and map how charge shifts near the boundary. They also test whether an extra lithium atom can enter the electrolyte. Entry proves unfavorable in most layers, suggesting Li3OCl stays stable against lithium metal.
arxiv-2604-10730: Rani, Cenko, and Cruz Castro survey undergraduate computing students on how generative AI changes the perceived importance of cognitive skills. Students rated 11 skills across three time frames: before widespread AI adoption, current informal and formal AI use in learning, and a future of deeper AI integration at work. Respondents expect all 11 skills to matter less in the future as AI use grows. The authors argue curricula need explicit interventions that reinforce cognitive skill development inside AI-reliant learning environments.
arxiv-2604-11030: Song and Mao study two conjectures for generalized off-diagonal Schur numbers. For positive integers, the generalized Schur number is the least positive integer such that every colouring of a range contains a monochromatic solution to a linear equation. In 2015, Ahmed and Schaal conjectured a formula for these numbers, and the authors confirm it. The same authors also conjectured a second formula, and motivated by it, Song and Mao give a recursive lower bound and upper bounds for all sufficiently large cases.
arxiv-2604-11130: Baştuğ proves a rigidity result for maps that place a compact shape into a complete manifold without stretching, in codimension one. Elastic energy here just measures how much a map stretches and bends its source. When a sequence of such maps has that energy fading to zero, a subsequence converges to a true distance-preserving map. The proof uses local rigidity estimates reduced to flat Euclidean space, avoiding Young measures and extending earlier work to targets that are not compact.
arxiv-2604-11330: Ghitza, Gupta, and Kortge tackle the inverse volcano problem over non-prime finite fields. Kohel showed isogeny graphs between ordinary elliptic curves form volcano-shaped components. Earlier work solved it completely over prime fields, with one counterexample over a squared prime field. The authors build a precise framework over general prime-power fields. Solvability typically hinges on volcano depth against the ell-valuation of the exponent. Small valuations yield infinitely many solving primes, while large valuations often make the problem unsolvable, with remaining cases conditional on modified Cohen-Lenstra heuristics.
arxiv-2604-11430: Stantchev hardens the x402 payment protocol against data leaks. Payment metadata in x402 requests reaches the payment server and central hub before on-chain settlement. Neither party is typically bound by a data deal. His open-source filter, presidio-hardened-x402, intercepts requests to redact personal data, enforce spending policies, and block replays. On a labeled synthetic set of 2,000 metadata triples, the best setup reaches micro-F1 0.894 with precision 0.972 at 5.73 milliseconds of 99th-percentile delay, within a 50-millisecond budget. The code, corpus, and tests are all public.
arxiv-2604-11730: González-González and ten colleagues explore deep learning for ambivalence and hesitancy recognition in videos for digital health. Ambivalence and hesitancy are subtle mixed feelings between positive and negative views or acceptance and refusal, making patients delay, avoid, or abandon care. They show up as mismatched feelings across or within channels like language, face, voice, and body. Experts can spot them, but adding them to digital care is costly. Automatic recognition is therefore key for tailored care, covering supervised learning, unsupervised domain adaptation, and zero-shot inference.
arxiv-2604-11930: Han, Kostina, and Hassibi study online linear-quadratic regulation under rate limits with unknown dynamics. Here, the plant sends learned dynamics estimates uplink for the controller to return the optimal policy. They prove any scheme with order-T-to-the-alpha regret, alpha between one half and one, must transmit at least order log-T bits. Their Quantized Certainty Equivalent algorithm matches that bound. Tests on four systems, up to a 24-parameter Boeing 747 model over 10,000 steps, confirm regret matching an unquantised baseline.
arxiv-2604-12430: Amit Pradhan generalizes a model of opinion-like interactions to groups of size q. The original Biswas-Chatterjee-Sen model used pairwise interactions only. Within a mean-field treatment, he derives the critical noise exactly. That threshold rises with group size and approaches one half for large groups. Yet the critical behavior stays unchanged across all group sizes. The order parameter and relaxation time scale just as in the original model. Finite-size scaling confirms mean-field Ising universality throughout.
arxiv-2604-12930: Kumar and Rao model how cells build and maintain compartments like the Golgi apparatus and endosomes amid constant membrane traffic. Their stochastic setup uses fusion and fission cycles that break detailed balance. It yields robust regimes from stable compartments to periodic dissolution and rebuilding tied to the cell cycle. The rival views of vesicular transport and cisternal progression emerge as two phases of one underlying process.
arxiv-2604-13030: Han and four colleagues introduce Generative Refinement Networks, a visual synthesis approach fixing two flaws at once. Diffusion models spend equal effort on all inputs, while autoregressive models lose detail to discrete tokens and piling errors. Their Hierarchical Binary Quantization keeps images near-lossless, and a global refinement step polishes outputs like a painter at a canvas. On ImageNet the system sets records at 0.56 rFID for reconstruction and 1.81 gFID for class-conditional generation.
arxiv-2604-13230: Olarte Rodríguez, Jankovic, Bäck, and Raponi ask whether random projections preserve landscape features used to describe black-box tuning problems. Working out exploratory landscape analysis features in reduced spaces and comparing them with original values. Across sample budgets and reduced sizes, they find linear random maps often distort the shape and topological structure that matters. A small subset of features stays fairly stable, but most prove highly touchy, and seeming toughness may reflect projection quirks rather than true traits.
arxiv-2604-13330: Tzavaras derives kinetic equations for systems with lasting oscillations. He covers two mechanics examples: Kelvin-Voigt viscoelasticity with double-well strain energies, used in phase transitions, and compressible Navier-Stokes for a barotropic gas. For each, he builds solutions with lasting oscillations. In short, both systems keep wobbling instead of settling down. He then shows, for the one-dimensional case and for the gas system, how those ideas yield simpler equations that couple one such equation with big-picture flow.
arxiv-2604-13630: Lin and ten colleagues secure the execution harness of language-model agents. That layer orchestrates tools, context, and state. Their SafeHarness design weaves four defenses into the agent lifecycle. These are adversarial context filtering, tiered causal verification, privilege-separated tool control, and safe rollback with adaptive degradation. Across benchmarks and attack scenarios, it cuts unsafe behavior by about 38 percent. Attack success falls by about 42 percent, while task utility holds.
arxiv-2604-13730: Khan and three colleagues bring continual learning to text-to-3D generation with ReConText3D. A model that learns new shapes should not forget old ones, yet existing models do. Their method keeps a compact, diverse replay memory. It is chosen by text-embedding k-Center selection, rehearsing prior knowledge without changing the base architecture. A new benchmark, Toys4K-CL, supplies balanced class-incremental splits. Across generative backbones, ReConText3D beats all baselines on old and new classes alike.
arxiv-2604-13930: Sun and colleagues simulate four years of Taiji observations of galactic double white dwarfs to test whether gravitational-wave microlensing can be detected. Within a Bayesian framework they estimate lens parameters and judge lensed against unlensed models. Lensing proves indistinguishable when the lens mass falls below 100,000 solar masses or the separation reaches three Einstein radii, though velocity effects remain separable across the tested range.
arxiv-2604-14130: Hu and Li tackle joint estimation of a linear system's dynamics and its noise covariance when noise need not be Gaussian. Their distributional framing parameterizes state transitions so the shape of the distribution, not just its center, informs the estimates. They offer two estimators, maximum likelihood and score matching, with proofs on accuracy and sample needs, and simulations show both beat ordinary least squares.
arxiv-2604-14230: Kaazempur-Mofrad, Dai, and He reframe interview allocation as a ranking problem under uncertainty, where departments pick from large pools with no signal of candidate leanings. They answer one survey on job traits, which hiring teams merge with files and hiring history to estimate acceptance odds and expected utilities. A confidence-calibrated ranking built on pairwise utility comparisons adds statistical guarantees, and the authors prove truthful participation is optimal. Against current practice, United States statistics department data show the framework lifts matching rates and quality and cuts hiring failures.
arxiv-2604-14430: Abu Ayyash presents the Three-Phase Transformer, a structural prior for decoders that splits the hidden vector into equal cyclic channels on a SwiGLU, RMSNorm, RoPE, and GQA backbone. Each channel keeps its own normalization, a two-dimensional rotation between attention and feed-forward, and a rule tying GQA heads to the split. A DC subspace orthogonal to the channels carries a fixed Gabriel's horn profile as an absolute-position side channel alongside RoPE. At 123 million parameters, perplexity falls 7.20 percent against a matched baseline, adding only 1,536 parameters.
arxiv-2604-14930: Lv and seven others propose IE-as-Cache, a framework that repurposes information extraction as a cognitive cache for agentic reasoning. Usually IE serves as a final goal, its results used alone rather than kept and reused across multi-step inference. Drawing on layered machine memory, the approach pairs query-driven extraction with cache-aware reasoning to maintain compact middle notes and filter noise. Tests on hard benchmarks across diverse language models show big thinking-accuracy gains, suggesting IE can serve as a mental resource for reuse in downstream thinking.
arxiv-2604-15030: Gibson and four others present a lackadaisical alternating walk with depth n squared plus n times t for n by n lattices over time. This cuts depth sharply versus the controlled walk, scaling as n squared times t, making it viable for noisy intermediate-scale devices. They use the walk as an entropy source for chaos-based key generation, producing reproducible bitstrings from its probability distribution with post-processing. Tests show reproducible 128-bit keys under IBM FakeTorino noise, and comparison with the controlled model highlights its cryptographic potential.
arxiv-2604-15430: Saurabh and five colleagues run the first 3D magnetic-fluid simulation of steady infall onto a horizonless singularity, a black-hole mimicker called JMN-1, where matter reaches the center instead of piling up outside. The flow settles into a magnetically held disk, and ray-traced images at 230 GHz broadly match Event Horizon Telescope views of M87*. Light from inside the observable shadow would betray JMN-1, a test for future radio telescopes.
arxiv-2604-15530: Lee implements sequential and non-sequential Zemax Dynamic Link Libraries that model image slicer integral field units from a known design in one file. Traditional multi-configuration modeling runs slowly, misses diffraction, and cannot fully describe an instrument in a single file. The new code copies native surface transforms exactly and rebuilds SPECTRE, a 36-slice lab spectrograph, with build-matched surface settings.
arxiv-2604-15630: Sanchez Sanchez introduces a force-free electrodynamics ansatz in flat spacetime under which the nonlinear system turns into a single semilinear wave equation in two variables. That cut yields explicit time-varying solutions, among them type-changing ones with finite energy per unit crosswise area and a null kink example. For traveling waves where magnetism rules, the field kernel pattern picks out minimal field-sheet layers.
arxiv-2604-15830: Fang and four colleagues propose PieceHint, a training framework that helps language models learn reasoning by giving hints exactly where they matter. Rather than handing out uniform partial solutions, it scores reasoning steps, places hints at bottlenecks matched to problem difficulty, then gradually withdraws support toward independent work. On six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, their 1.5B model matched much larger 32B baselines on average while preserving diverse correct answers.
arxiv-2604-16030: Kanellopoulos and three colleagues study finite k-Visits Pinwheel Scheduling, asking whether length k times n schedules can run each task k times without a deadline expiring between visits. They prove 2-Visits is strongly NP-complete even at maximum multiplicity 2, settling an open question. They also prove 2-Visits lies in RP for constant distinct deadlines, advancing another open question. Results generalize to a mixed version, though 3-Visits transfer looks unlikely. They bound thresholds, with a lower bound above nine tenths for 2-Visits and a k-Visits threshold approaching five sixths.
arxiv-2604-16330: Achkar, Gollub, and Potthast present SR4CS, a large set of systematic reviews in CS. Systematic reviews sum up evidence, but building them takes heavy manual work in search and screening. Existing testing tools sit mostly in health, blocking shared work elsewhere. SR4CS holds 1,212 reviews with expert Boolean search queries, 104,316 settled sources, and ordered methods notes. Early tests compare expert queries with zero-shot LLM-made Boolean queries.
arxiv-2604-16530: Mohammady presents a frame for sizing Riemann zeta values. He sets a whole-sum change against local changes of each term. Their gap defines a shortfall measure that yields a match. Sizing that deficit follows, with bias fixed and a law for how errors close. For odd targets, base choices recover the cutoff rate while keeping the match. Tests on zeta at 3, 5 and 7 confirm the theory and extend to spectral zeta functions, giving a viewpoint, not a swap for methods.
arxiv-2604-16830: Zhang and colleagues show on-policy distillation lifts task accuracy while trapping models in severe overconfidence. Teacher supervision uses hidden training context, but live models must report confidence from live data alone. Teacher-led success is therefore not a valid trust target, and hidden context induces entropy collapse and bias. CaOPD gauges seen trust from rollouts, swaps self-told trust with that student-grounded target, and distills the revised reply. Across models and domains, CaOPD reaches Pareto-optimal calibration with strong capability, generalizing under shift and ongoing learning.
arxiv-2604-16930: Zeng, Lu, and Wang guide expert selection in visual question answering with the meaning of the answer options themselves, steadying choices that otherwise flip between similar questions. Their CoGR-MoE framework reweights chosen experts with option features. It sharpens option comparisons through contrastive learning, reporting strong results across several visual question answering tasks.
arxiv-2604-17130: Furmanczyk and Paczutkowski tackle PU classification when the SCAR condition, which says labeled positives are a random sample of all positives, fails to hold. Their cluster-cleaning method first draws cleaning labels from two-means clustering, then runs logistic regression on the cleaned data with extra true positives added. Tested on eleven real datasets plus a synthetic set, it works where SCAR is violated, and the LassoJoint method proves fairly robust to SCAR perturbations.
arxiv-2604-17230: Sharma, Majumdar, and Sachdeva revisit a proposed way of making cosmic magnetic fields from ultralight dark matter, in which fields amplify through resonance driven by the oscillating pseudoscalar field. Earlier analysis ignored the plasma; the authors add finite plasma conductivity to the pseudoscalar and electromagnetic fields. Because conductivity is large next to the Hubble parameter, resonance growth is sharply suppressed. For viable coupling values, the way cannot make fields strong enough to explain those seen in cosmic voids.
arxiv-2604-17330: Lorincik and five colleagues analyze the 2022 March 31 solar flare using IRIS ultraviolet and STIX X-ray observations, chasing the link between pulsing flare ribbons and three-dimensional magnetic reconnection. STIX caught nonthermal pulses about 35 seconds apart from two steady footpoints, mostly matching ultraviolet pulses in the same ribbon areas. Slipping ribbon kernels tracked the pulses less closely, suggesting the strongest electron energy landed in one loop system inside a larger reconnecting structure.
arxiv-2604-17430: Marciniak, Olechowski, and Pokorski test alpha-attractor P-models of cosmic inflation against microwave background data. Here the reheating temperature follows straight from observed quantities, so bounds that hold for any model narrow the allowed ranges. They survey many polynomial potentials, with inflaton decay and breakup during reheating taken into account. Predictions for the spectral index and tensor-to-scalar ratio fit Planck data and Planck plus ACT data, though results shift with reheating temperature and the ratio bound.
arxiv-2604-17930: Renduchintala and Bhatia test whether language models fail some grammar patterns from architecture limits or simply from scarce examples in web text. They pretrain small GPT-2 models on a 100-million-token FineWeb sample, injecting just 1 percent synthetic data aimed at specific phenomena. Targeted data lifts performance in eight of nine worst BLiMP paradigms, with one paradigm jumping from 20.9 percent to 69.4 percent accuracy. One resistant pattern stays below chance, yet the result shows data composition, not just scale, can repair many linguistic gaps.
arxiv-2604-18130: Asikis and Nax invert the usual laboratory approach to double auctions. In these markets, buyers and sellers post bids and asks, but posted prices do not reveal true reservation values. The authors therefore train models on quantile-normalized bids, asks, and realized prices. Their models predict allocative efficiency early, with accuracy improving as more trades arrive, offering a tool for governing real digital marketplaces.
arxiv-2604-18630: Sole treats chart choice in performance study as shaping findings, not a neutral display step, since each form shows traits others hide. He sets out five tools that work together: tempographs, combination charts, histograms, ridgeline plots, and stacked bar charts. He tries them on beat-level tempo data from Beethoven's five piano-cello sonatas from 1930 to 2012. Each tool gets a formal sketch and a note on what it shows. He tests them on two Opus 5 Number 1 takes: Casals with Horszowski from the 1930s and Isserlis with Levin from 2012.
arxiv-2604-18730: Casavecchia and four colleagues model oxygen-III light from early star-forming galaxies, using a post-processing pipeline inside SPICE simulations of gas and radiation. Three supernova feedback recipes are compared: bursty, smooth, and hypernova-based. The light comes mainly from shock-heated gas lit up by radiation. The bursty recipe ionizes gas well but adds metals less well by redshift 5, leaving fewer bright emitters than the smooth recipe, so oxygen-III light proves a sharp tracer of stellar feedback.
arxiv-2604-19230: Knook, Baier-Reinio, and Farrell work on solving diffusion equations faster. They build preconditioners, speed-ups for hard equation systems, for the Onsager-Stefan-Maxwell equations. They propose an augmented Lagrangian version and prove it stays strong as the mesh is refined. For Newton linearization it serves as a block smoother inside geometric multigrid. The strategy handles mixed-species flows and several heat, pressure, and charge effects.
arxiv-2604-19330: Ma and Cartwright extend the coarse-to-fine idea in text-to-speech synthesis into the time domain with Chain-of-Details. Their cascaded framework refines temporal detail stage by stage, with each stage aimed at a specific time granularity. All detail predictions share one decoder, which keeps parameter use efficient across resolutions. Notably, the coarsest level plans phonetics on its own, with no separate phoneme duration predictor, and the method is tested on several datasets.
arxiv-2604-19430: Cotellucci and Giusti present an update from the BMW Collaboration on isospin-breaking effects in the pion decay constant. The computation uses staggered quarks with a near-physical pion mass and a finite-volume quantum electrodynamics setup. The paper updates the isosymmetric value and the current determination used for the gradient-flow scale. It also gives preliminary results for the valence-valence part of the axial-pseudoscalar correlator across volumes and lattice spacings, and discusses next steps.
arxiv-2604-19630: Weitsman proves that graphs of solutions to the minimal surface equation over simply connected domains with boundary values 0 can have at most exponential growth. A minimal graph comes from a function whose surface minimizes area locally, like a soap film spanning a boundary. The theorem bounds how fast such a graph can grow as the domain expands. Simply connected means the domain has no holes, and boundary values 0 fix the graph at the domain edge.
arxiv-2604-19730: Dong, Swerdlow, Sadigh, and Finn present FASTER, a way to gain the benefits of sampling-based test-time scaling for diffusion policies without paying the full compute cost. Top reinforcement learning methods sample many action candidates and pick the best. But that selection step is expensive at run time. FASTER traces the gain back to earlier in the denoising process, modeling candidate filtering as a Markov decision process and learning a policy and value function in denoising space.
arxiv-2604-20230: Wang and six colleagues predict crystal structures with heat and nuclear quantum effects, via deep free energy learning. The harmonic free energy surface shares the shape of a potential energy surface, so a deep neural net potential learns it directly. A two-level concurrent learning workflow builds the model, giving energies, forces, and stresses in one forward pass. At 200 GPa and 300 K it matches seen LaH10 and LaSc2H24 phases and finds a new stable clathrate hydride, LaScH8. Its cost runs more than a million fold below DFT-level rivals.
arxiv-2604-20330: Beslikas studies composition operators on weighted Bergman spaces over the bidisc, induced by rational inner functions or a rational inner function plus a smooth function. His main result gives one uniform criterion for every beta from just above minus one to zero: boundedness matches transversal intersection of level sets for non-smooth symbols. Tangential intersections on the singularity, when they occur, must be of high order. The criterion extends a Bayart-Kosiński characterization to non-smooth self maps of the bidisc, using Clark measures and Puiseux factorizations.
arxiv-2604-20430: Cavallina and Pinamonti study a parabolic version of Serrin's overdetermined problem, where the constant flux condition holds only at a discrete infinite set of time values. Under suitable regularity assumptions, they show such a problem admits a solution exactly when the domain is a ball. Depending on the time scale, the same condition captures geometric or spectral information, yet both routes lead to the same rigidity conclusion. They treat flux on the boundary and on an interior surface alike, and extend the problem to complete Riemannian manifolds.
arxiv-2604-20630: Bagmar and Shen develop a doubly robust weighted regression tool for causal inference when confounders are missing. Old missing-flag methods rely on a single model, working only when that model is right. MI-WOLS blends propensity-score weighting into outcome regression, with balancing weights covering confounders and their missingness flags. Under either an independent treatment or outcome structure, MI-WOLS needs only one of the two models to be right. Tests show tiny bias, good variance figures, and near-nominal coverage across many cases.
arxiv-2604-21230: Hong-Bo Huang and Hui Dong solve the fastest possible reset for a frequency-tunable qubit coupled to a structured environment. Fast reuse clashes with the weak decoherence good computation needs. Their switch-restore-switch sequence moves the qubit from a calm computational setting to a strongly dissipative restoring setting and back. For superconducting qubits in four representative environments, reset time falls from typically over 100 nanoseconds to 20 nanoseconds, about 40 percent of a typical two-qubit gate time.
arxiv-2604-21330: Masahiro Kada and four colleagues stabilize sparse mixture-of-experts routing for vision models, where the router learns only through experts chosen in the forward pass. That gradient blocking leaves unselected routes uninformative, breeding unstable, fluctuating assignments. Their TGR-MoE method builds a teacher router from a pretrained dense teacher's intermediate representations and uses its outputs as pseudo-supervision for the student router. On ImageNet-1K and CIFAR-100 it improves accuracy and routing consistency, holding stable even under highly sparse settings.
arxiv-2604-21630: Melchior Wirth settles a conjecture about how quickly quantum Markov semigroups decay, comparing decay rates measured with two different inner products, named KMS and GNS. He proves the KMS rate always sits at or above the GNS rate. The result holds far beyond Gaussian examples, reaching semigroups on general von Neumann algebras that preserve a single well-behaved steady state. The argument extends the KMS product to a wider family built from operator monotone functions.
arxiv-2604-21830: Holeczek and four colleagues present GFlowState, a visual analytics system for the training of Generative Flow Networks, which sample in proportion to a reward function. Standard tools track metrics but hide how models explore sample space, build trajectories, or shift sampling odds during training. GFlowState offers a candidate-ranking chart, a state projection, a node-link diagram of the trajectory network, and a transition heatmap. Case studies show it helps developers debug training, spot underexplored regions, and judge model quality.
arxiv-2604-22030: Neumann and three colleagues study student use of generative AI tools in computing courses and develop a framework for institutional adaptation to GenAI usage. The authors ran a case study at Hannover's University of Applied Sciences and Arts, mixing records review with a survey of 151 business and e-government students. Generative AI uptake was broad, with ChatGPT the leading tool. Students mainly used generative AI for research help, coding help, and text work. Many students did not know or were unsure about institutional generative AI rules.
arxiv-2604-22530: Peng presents DEKL 2.0, a type-theory framework for knowledge evolving along traces, step records of a system. Its central claim splits behavior in two: the proof calculus stays monotone under standard rules, while non-monotone change arises in meaning when traces extend. Finite and infinite traces count as first-class objects, and knowledge is read as a presheaf over the finite-trace category. The paper establishes trace-reachability and completeness, characterizes non-monotonicity through non-surjective restriction maps, and interprets the system via a free category from a transition system.
arxiv-2604-22630: Liu and three colleagues give the first non-trivial bootstrap percolation bound for complete graphs. The F-bootstrap process adds edges completing copies of F, and the running time is the step where it stops changing. Bollobás posed the running time problem for n vertices. Until now the best bound for complete graphs on t vertices, with t at least 5, was the trivial pairs bound. Running time is a fraction of pairs approaching one from below as t grows, for t at least 3. A k-graph result follows.
arxiv-2604-22730: Mutisya and Mugane ask whether neural models trained only on modern Bantu word forms can recover vocabulary structure matching historical reconstruction. Using BantuMorph v7 across fourteen Eastern and Southern Bantu languages, they extract noun and verb cognate candidates and check them against reconstructed Proto-Bantu forms. Ten of the top eleven noun candidates align, including words for person and cow.
arxiv-2604-22930: Dzib and eleven colleagues use VLBA observations to measure dynamical masses of young stellar systems in Orion. Their survey covers 19 radio sources across 15 binary or multiple systems. For four binaries with both stars detected, Keplerian orbits give model-independent masses, with two systems matching spectral-energy-distribution estimates. One component, NU Ori C, is confirmed as an intermediate-mass star with nonthermal radio emission, hinting at magnetic activity near the high-mass boundary, while other sources point to unseen partners.
arxiv-2604-23130: Das and three colleagues trace jailbreak weakness in safety-aligned language models to small, prompt-linked groups of Sparse Autoencoder features, not broad refusal directions. With Gemma-2-2B and single-category unsafe cases from BeaverTails, they pull harmful concepts from adversarial replies and match them to prompt tokens. Three grouping methods across all 26 layers find vulnerable feature groups, strongest in mid-to-late layers. Amplifying the top features, single-token grouping matches full cluster grouping on harm, showing that single harmful tokens can pinpoint where steering breaks safety.
arxiv-2604-23230: Ali analyses how a financial-technology organisation puts ISO/IEC 27001:2022 into practice across eight procedures, from risk assessment and access control to backup management and corrective action. Drawing on internal training materials, the study checks each procedure against Annex A controls and Clauses 6 to 10. It weighs the CIA Triad as a test, a twelve-step risk method, role-based responsibility, and corrective action's link to continual improvement. The findings point to a tight, multi-layered hierarchy with clear accountability and measurable risk metrics as the base of effective implementation.
arxiv-2604-23330: Bertschinger and five colleagues study common intersections of double-wedge arrangements mixing bowties and hourglasses, which differ on vertical lines. A point in the intersection equals a line stabbing one segment set while avoiding another, a duality shift that breaks earlier bowtie-only arguments. In this general setting, the intersection of n double-wedges can split into quadratically many interior-disjoint regions. They also give Gallai-type results for segment and anti-segment arrangements, plus optimal intersection algorithms and a near-optimal single-point finder.
arxiv-2604-23430: Shahi and Hummel test whether ready-made large language models can sort scientific papers into a hierarchical subject taxonomy, trying plain examples and chained prompts. Chained prompting beats examples alone, especially for the nested structure, and tops older specialist models at the broad domain and subject levels. At the finest topic level, however, accuracy reaches only about half even with the best prompting.
arxiv-2604-23630: Dhote and colleagues study how surface tension steers thin elastic plates floating in surface gravity waves. Such floaters drift toward one of two preferred orientations, along the wave direction or along the wave crests, and the team models the mean turning force with capillary effects included. Orientation hinges on a single parameter comparing wavelength, floater length, and immersion depth against a critical value, and experiments with metal plates agree.
arxiv-2604-23830: Shalawadi and colleagues analyse user reactions to AI-generated fitness feedback on Strava, drawing on 297 discussion threads and over 5,600 comments. They find four recurring tensions: numbers versus context, single sessions versus training narratives, fixed AI tone versus varied emotions, and one AI voice versus diverse athlete types. Across all four, users resist feedback that narrows their own interpretation of lived experience, pointing to design that preserves interpretive openness.
arxiv-2604-24430: Amestoy and three colleagues present a data-driven method for joint prior selection in linear mixed models. Bayesian frameworks need good priors, often missing in advance, above all for random-effect covariances. Their empirical Bayes method picks priors by best fit, using a fast Laplace approximation. Simulations show much better parameter estimates and forecasts. A real air pollution and health dataset shows the method supports richer, sounder models with better predictive results.
arxiv-2604-24530: Liu, Tang, Wang and Zhang study a second-price auction where the seller designs bidder signals that are independent beforehand, called private private information, while valuations share a correlated prior. They show full surplus extraction can be implemented in equilibrium, though that equilibrium may be unstable. A second construction gets revenue arbitrarily close to maximum welfare with a strict equilibrium. Yet bidder surplus in general cannot reach maximum welfare exactly.
